## Question

In run A (notebooks 04–06), NOTCH1 on the lymphoid side was not linked to the four Notch targets we chose (HES1,
DTX1, NRARP, PTCRA), and the targets followed the lymphoid population instead. Single target genes are sparse in
single-cell data, and the four were picked by hand. Here we replace them with **one score per cell** computed from a
published gene set, and ask whether this score behaves like a measure of Notch activity before it is used in run C
(stroma → ETP + DN(early)):

1. Which genes does a database give as Notch targets, and how many are detected in our cells?
2. Is the score higher in the early T-lineage populations (Notch-dependent) than in NK cells and ILC3?
3. Does the score follow sequencing depth within each population, more than a random gene set of the same kind?
4. Within ETP and DN(early) (the receivers of run C), how does the score vary with population and donor?

**Choices and their sources.**

- *Gene set.* Notch receptors act through the DNA-binding factor RBPJ (CSL): the cleaved Notch intracellular domain
  binds RBPJ and turns its targets on (Kopan & Ilagan, *Cell* 2009,
  [doi:10.1016/j.cell.2009.03.045](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.cell.2009.03.045)). The Notch target set is the RBPJ
  regulon of **CollecTRI** (Müller-Dott *et al.*, *Nucleic Acids Res* 2023,
  [doi:10.1093/nar/gkad841](https://doi.org/10.1093/nar/gkad841)), a curated collection of signed transcription
  factor → target interactions with literature references (file: `data/README.md`). PROGENy (Schubert *et al.*,
  *Nat Commun* 2018) has no Notch pathway, so it cannot be used here.
- *Score.* **AUCell** (Aibar *et al.*, *Nat Methods* 2017, [doi:10.1038/nmeth.4463](https://doi.org/10.1038/nmeth.4463))
  ranks the genes within each cell and measures how many genes of the set are near the top. It uses only ranks within
  a cell, so it is less tied to the total counts than a sum of counts – our main confounder in runs A and B.

## Setup

```{r}
#| label: setup
#| message: false
#| warning: false

library(tidyverse)
library(Matrix)
library(AUCell)

find_repo_root <- function(dir = getwd()) {
  while (!(file.exists(file.path(dir, "README.md")) && dir.exists(file.path(dir, "notebooks")))) {
    parent <- dirname(dir)
    if (parent == dir) stop("Repository root not found. Open the repository folder in Positron.")
    dir <- parent
  }
  dir
}
root <- find_repo_root()

data_dir <- file.path(root, "data", "thymus")
res_dir  <- file.path(root, "results", "thymus_early")
out_dir  <- file.path(res_dir, "10_activity_scores")
fig_dir  <- file.path(root, "results", "figures", "thymus_early")
dir.create(out_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
dir.create(fig_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

populations <- c("ETP", "DN(early)", "DN(P)", "DN(Q)", "γδT", "NK", "ILC3",   # early lymphoid
                 "cTEC", "mTEC(II)", "Fb_1", "Endo")                       # stroma
```

The cells are those exported for run A (notebook 04): all 11 populations of 7–11 PCW, at most 500 cells per
population (seed 0), raw counts. ETP (127 cells) and DN(early) (201) are complete, so run C can use the same cells.

```{r}
#| label: cells

input_dir <- file.path(res_dir, "04_runA_input")
counts <- readMM(file.path(input_dir, "counts.mtx.gz"))               # genes x cells
genes  <- read_csv(file.path(input_dir, "genes.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE)$gene
cells  <- read_csv(file.path(input_dir, "cells.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE) |>
  mutate(population = factor(population, levels = populations))
dimnames(counts) <- list(genes, cells$cell)
counts <- as(counts, "CsparseMatrix")
cells$n_detected <- colSums(counts > 0)

count(cells, group, population)
```

## 1. The gene set

CollecTRI gives each RBPJ → target interaction a sign. AUCell ignores signs, so only targets that RBPJ **activates**
are kept (`is_stimulation` true and `is_inhibition` false); repressed and ambiguous targets would lower the score of
cells where Notch is active.

```{r}
#| label: regulon

collectri <- read_tsv(file.path(data_dir, "collectri", "collectri_human.tsv"), show_col_types = FALSE)

rbpj <- collectri |>
  filter(source_genesymbol == "RBPJ") |>
  summarise(stimulation = any(is_stimulation), inhibition = any(is_inhibition),
            curation_effort = max(curation_effort), .by = target_genesymbol) |>
  rename(gene = target_genesymbol) |>
  mutate(sign = case_when(stimulation & !inhibition ~ "activated",
                          inhibition & !stimulation ~ "repressed",
                          .default = "both"))
count(rbpj, sign)
```

Two more filters:

- **No ligand or receptor gene.** In run C, ligands and receptors are network variables and the L–R links are imposed.
  A score that contains NOTCH1 or DLL4 would be partly the same measurement as the receptor. Every gene of every partner
  of table S5 (complexes split into their subunits with the CellPhoneDB v2 files, as in notebook 04) is removed.
- **Present in the count matrix** (gene symbols of the atlas).

```{r}
#| label: lr-genes

db <- file.path(data_dir, "cellphonedb_v2_db", "db_2019-09")
gene_db <- read_csv(file.path(db, "gene_input.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE) |>
  distinct(uniprot, .keep_all = TRUE) |>
  mutate(gene_name = recode(gene_name, NECTIN1 = "PVRL1", NECTIN2 = "PVRL2", NECTIN3 = "PVRL3"))
complexes <- read_csv(file.path(db, "complex_input.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE) |>
  pivot_longer(uniprot_1:uniprot_4, values_to = "uniprot", values_drop_na = TRUE) |>
  left_join(gene_db, by = "uniprot") |>
  select(complex_name, gene_name)

s5 <- read_csv(file.path(res_dir, "03_ligand_receptor_candidates", "s5_oriented.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE)
partners <- unique(c(s5$ligand, s5$receptor))
lr_genes <- unique(c(setdiff(partners, complexes$complex_name),
                     complexes$gene_name[complexes$complex_name %in% partners]))
stopifnot(!anyNA(lr_genes))
length(lr_genes)
```

```{r}
#| label: gene-set

rbpj <- rbpj |>
  mutate(kept = case_when(sign != "activated" ~ paste(sign, "target"),
                          gene %in% lr_genes ~ "ligand or receptor (table S5)",
                          !gene %in% genes ~ "not in the count matrix",
                          .default = "kept"))
count(rbpj, kept)
filter(rbpj, kept == "ligand or receptor (table S5)")$gene
notch_set <- sort(filter(rbpj, kept == "kept")$gene)
```

How often each kept gene is detected, in the run C receivers (ETP + DN(early)) and in the other groups:

```{r}
#| label: detection

cell_group <- case_when(cells$population %in% c("ETP", "DN(early)") ~ "ETP + DN(early)",
                        cells$population %in% c("DN(P)", "DN(Q)") ~ "DN(P) + DN(Q)",
                        cells$population %in% c("NK", "ILC3") ~ "NK + ILC3",
                        cells$population == "γδT" ~ "γδT",
                        .default = "stroma")
detected <- map(split(seq_len(ncol(counts)), cell_group),
                \(j) rowMeans(counts[notch_set, j, drop = FALSE] > 0)) |>
  as_tibble() |>
  mutate(gene = notch_set, .before = 1) |>
  select(gene, `ETP + DN(early)`, `DN(P) + DN(Q)`, `γδT`, `NK + ILC3`, stroma) |>
  arrange(desc(`ETP + DN(early)`))

c(genes_in_set = length(notch_set),
  detected_in_5pct_of_ETP_DNearly = sum(detected$`ETP + DN(early)` >= 0.05),
  never_detected_in_these_cells = sum(rowSums(counts[notch_set, ] > 0) == 0))
detected |> head(25) |> mutate(across(where(is.numeric), \(x) round(x, 2)))
```

## 2. Scoring

AUCell ranks the genes of each cell; genes with the same value (most of them at 0) are put in random order, hence the
seed. The score looks only at the top `aucMaxRank` genes of each ranking. The AUCell vignette asks that most cells
detect at least that many genes; otherwise the end of the window falls among random zeros. The default (5% of 33,694
genes = 1,685) is above the number of genes detected by `r round(100 * mean(cells$n_detected < 1685))`% of the cells,
so the window is set to the **10th percentile of detected genes**: 90% of the cells have at least that many.

```{r}
#| label: auc

quantile(cells$n_detected, c(0.05, 0.1, 0.25, 0.5))
max_rank <- floor(quantile(cells$n_detected, 0.1))
max_rank

set.seed(0)
rankings <- AUCell_buildRankings(counts, plotStats = FALSE, splitByBlocks = TRUE, verbose = FALSE)
notch_auc <- getAUC(AUCell_calcAUC(list(notch = notch_set), rankings, aucMaxRank = max_rank, verbose = FALSE))
cells$notch_auc <- notch_auc["notch", cells$cell]
```

**Control gene sets.** A score can differ between populations simply because some populations detect more genes
(median `r min(tapply(cells$n_detected, cells$population, median))` to
`r max(tapply(cells$n_detected, cells$population, median))` here). To see what is specific to the Notch set, the same
score is computed for 100 random gene sets of the same size, in which each Notch gene is replaced by a random gene
detected in a similar fraction of cells (same twentieth of the detection distribution). The **adjusted score** is the
Notch score minus the mean score of the random sets in the same cell.

```{r}
#| label: control-sets

detection <- rowMeans(counts > 0)
pool <- names(detection)[detection > 0 & !names(detection) %in% c(notch_set, lr_genes)]
bins <- cut(detection, breaks = unique(quantile(detection[pool], seq(0, 1, 0.05))), include.lowest = TRUE)
names(bins) <- names(detection)

set.seed(1)
control_sets <- map(1:100, \(i) map_chr(notch_set, \(g) {
  same_bin <- pool[bins[pool] == bins[g]]
  if (length(same_bin) == 0 || is.na(bins[g])) same_bin <- pool    # genes never detected: any gene
  sample(same_bin, 1)
}))
names(control_sets) <- paste0("control_", 1:100)
control_matrix <- getAUC(AUCell_calcAUC(control_sets, rankings, aucMaxRank = max_rank, verbose = FALSE))

cells$control_auc <- colMeans(control_matrix[, cells$cell])
cells$notch_adjusted <- cells$notch_auc - cells$control_auc
```

## 3. Is the score higher where Notch is expected to be active?

Notch signalling specifies the T lineage in thymic progenitors and is needed up to β-selection; in human thymus it is
active in CD34⁺ progenitors and developing thymocytes (García-León *et al.*, *Development* 2018,
[doi:10.1242/dev.165597](https://doi.org/10.1242/dev.165597)), and strong Notch signals also favour γδ T cells
(Van de Walle *et al.*, *J Exp Med* 2013, [doi:10.1084/jem.20121798](https://doi.org/10.1084/jem.20121798)).
Expected: ETP, DN(early), DN(P), DN(Q) and γδT above NK and ILC3. The stroma is not a negative control: endothelial
cells use Notch signalling themselves.

```{r}
#| label: by-population

by_population <- cells |>
  summarise(cells = n(), notch_auc = median(notch_auc), control_auc = median(control_auc),
            notch_adjusted = median(notch_adjusted), .by = population) |>
  arrange(population)
by_population |> mutate(across(c(notch_auc, control_auc, notch_adjusted), \(x) signif(x, 2)))
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-score
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 4.5

plot_data <- cells |>
  select(population, group, `Notch set` = notch_auc, `random sets (mean)` = control_auc,
         `adjusted (Notch − random)` = notch_adjusted) |>
  pivot_longer(-c(population, group), names_to = "score") |>
  mutate(score = fct_inorder(score))
p <- ggplot(plot_data, aes(population, value, fill = group)) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.size = 0.3) +
  facet_wrap(~score, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(stroma = "#b5d99c", early_lymphoid = "#f2c57c"),
                    labels = c(stroma = "stroma", early_lymphoid = "early lymphoid")) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "AUCell score", fill = NULL,
       title = "Notch (RBPJ regulon, CollecTRI) activity score by population, 7–11 PCW") +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1), legend.position = "bottom")
p
ggsave(file.path(fig_dir, "10_notch_score_by_population.png"), p, width = 10, height = 4.5, dpi = 150)
```

## 4. Does the score follow sequencing depth?

Within each population, Spearman correlation of each score with the total counts of the cell (`n_counts`). For the
random sets, the median correlation over the 100 sets.

```{r}
#| label: depth

depth <- cells |>
  summarise(cells = n(),
            notch = cor(notch_auc, n_counts, method = "spearman"),
            random_sets_median = median(apply(control_matrix[, cell, drop = FALSE], 1,
                                              \(a) cor(a, n_counts, method = "spearman"))),
            adjusted = cor(notch_adjusted, n_counts, method = "spearman"),
            .by = population) |>
  arrange(population)
depth |> mutate(across(where(is.double), \(x) round(x, 2)))
```

## 5. Within the run C receivers

```{r}
#| label: run-c-receivers

receivers <- filter(cells, population %in% c("ETP", "DN(early)")) |> droplevels()
receivers |>
  summarise(cells = n(), notch_auc = median(notch_auc), notch_adjusted = median(notch_adjusted),
            .by = c(population, donor)) |>
  arrange(population, desc(cells)) |>
  mutate(across(c(notch_auc, notch_adjusted), \(x) signif(x, 2)))

wilcox.test(notch_adjusted ~ population, data = receivers)$p.value
kruskal.test(notch_adjusted ~ donor, data = filter(receivers, population == "DN(early)"))$p.value
```

## 6. Export

```{r}
#| label: export

rbpj |>
  select(gene, sign, curation_effort, kept) |>
  arrange(kept != "kept", gene) |>
  write_csv(file.path(out_dir, "notch_gene_set.csv"))
cells |>
  select(cell, population, donor, n_counts, n_detected, notch_auc, control_auc, notch_adjusted) |>
  write_csv(file.path(out_dir, "notch_scores.csv"))
writeLines(c(paste("aucMaxRank:", max_rank), paste("genes in the Notch set:", length(notch_set))),
           file.path(out_dir, "settings.txt"))
list.files(out_dir)
```

## Summary

| Question | Result |
| -------- | ------ |
| 1. Gene set | CollecTRI gives 155 RBPJ targets; 105 are activated, 89 remain after removing 16 ligand/receptor genes (NOTCH1–3, DLL4, CD40, …). 50 of the 89 are detected in ≥ 5% of ETP + DN(early) cells. |
| 2. Positive control | **Fails.** ETP and DN(early) have the lowest scores of the lymphoid populations (median adjusted score 0.009 and 0.012), below NK (0.013) and ILC3 (0.021); DN(P) and DN(Q) are the highest (0.025, 0.029). |
| 3. Sequencing depth | Within populations, the raw score correlates with `n_counts` from −0.13 to 0.29; random sets of matched detection from −0.29 to −0.16. Subtracting them makes the dependence on depth stronger (0.05 to 0.40), not weaker. |
| 4. Run C receivers | The score differs between ETP and DN(early) (Wilcoxon p = 0.02) and strongly between donors within DN(early) (Kruskal–Wallis p = 1.5 × 10⁻⁸). |

**Why the score fails.** The CollecTRI regulon collects RBPJ targets reported in any tissue. The 89 genes include
pancreatic (PDX1, PTF1A), neural (SOX2, NEUROG1), erythroid (HBB, AHSP) and T-helper (IL17A, FOXP3, TBX21) genes, and
broadly expressed genes (DUSP1, MT2A, CDK6, REL, NFKB1, NFKB2). The genes most often detected in our cells are of the
last kind. The known T-lineage Notch targets are only 6 of the 89 (HES1, DTX1, NRARP, PTCRA, GATA3, TCF7). Taken one
at a time, they do follow the expected pattern (for example DTX1 is detected in 34% of ETP + DN(early) cells and 3% of
NK + ILC3), but the rest of the set hides them.

**Consequence.** This score is not used in run C. A Notch score for thymocytes would need a gene set measured in
human T-lineage cells (for example genes that respond to Notch ligands in human CD34⁺ progenitors), which no database
used here provides.
